title: Indefinite quadratic division and affine characteristic parameters
source_hypothesis: Smooth homogeneous complex symbol satisfying P; compact embedded regular one-dimensional characteristic meeting the indefinite transverse Hessian set. Ordinary tubes include radial motion. The affine quotient may have endpoints from terminal zero tails.
reviewed_arguments: The ordinary compact complex tube is proved with an extended nonzero multiplier, exact smooth division and canonical transverse transport. It retains the prescribed parameter and covers radial arcs.

Two parameter Morse reductions expose opposite quadratic directions. Even/odd smooth extension and integral divided differences prove exact quadratic division with all parameters on one common compact-time neighborhood.

Two real-root tests give complementary remainder supports. Every derivative of both remainders vanishes on the intervening parameter-zero set; the finite Taylor order of the divisor forces the full quotient jets to agree.

Distance-to-zero-set Taylor bounds prove smooth pasting across an arbitrary singular closed set. The actual quotient is nonnegative by the sign condition and density, normalized to one at the reference time, and has the required homogeneous extension.
Indefinite points are excluded from both the rank-two saturation and the escaping set by exact earlier normal forms and Hessian invariance. Their regular characteristic continuation is retained.

A complex linear variational equation defines the symplectic normal transport. The kernel and radical are preserved; coordinate changes, nonzero complex multipliers and regular reparametrizations give exactly the same quotient connection.

The imaginary Hessian descends to the quotient and has the exact multiplier and time transformation laws. Bilinear transpose identities prove transported proportionality and the indefinite-or-zero alternative.

The nonnegative scalar defines an affine primitive. The proof includes quotient topology, bounded zero intervals, terminal zero tails, affine chart transitions, periodic local charts and the distinction from the original smooth structure at isolated zeros.

Three solved exercises give an exact nilpotent transport through a flat interval, a homogeneous radial characteristic with affine coordinate minus its radial momentum, and the correctly normalized parameter-change factor.

The general semidefinite nonnegative quotient remains explicitly unfinished. The one-sided smooth remainder is proved, and the previously delivered rank obstruction is preserved; no full Section 26.5 completion is claimed.
Twenty-five exact identities passed. All reader captures and the figure were inspected, the crossing figure labels were repaired, and all display extents were measured on desktop and mobile.
